title: field-play-scripts-llm-endpoints-playbook
content:
Purpose and intended use:
- Quick field playbook for AEs/SDRs/SEs to run concise, pragmatic conversations vs LLM endpoint vendors.
- Focus: product-led differentiation (serve economics, predictable SLAs, private deployments), trap detection, and short scripts to win meetings and pilot decisions.
- This is a living working doc: copy into customer-specific play and annotate with measurements from our tableau/benchmarks.

How to use in a call (30/60/90 second hooks):
- 30s opener: We help teams keep inference predictable and cost-effective as model choice changes. Focus on throughput, burst behavior, and private control plane.
- 60s value prop: If you care about latency, unit cost, and predictable budgets — we provide Dedicated and Private deployments with tooling to tune batching, KV caching, and quantize profiles so your app stays on-SLA without sacrificing quality.
- 90s pilot close: Offer a 2-week performance proof: cost-per-1k tokens baseline vs our tuned config + a private test endpoint.

Competitor themes to expect and traps to call out (quick detection):
- 'Lowest baseline price': Often advertised but excludes memory/latency variability and burst pricing. Ask for end-to-end cost per useful token at 95th percentile latency and for sustained throughput.
- 'Just use our hosted model': Probe on private data, compliance, and inflection points when they recommend self-hosting. Many vendors treat private as an afterthought, not a product.
- 'Autoscaling takes care of it': Real autoscaling without predictable latency SLOs is rare. Ask what the guarantee is for cold-starts, queueing, and tail latency.
- 'We have a higher-quality model': Ask for benchmark prompts and share your eval set. Quality claims without regression monitoring are brittle.

Quick competitor-specific call scripts (one-liners + follow-ups):
- Competitor: Open-style hosted endpoints
  - Script: We love hosted endpoints for quick proofs, but when teams scale they run into burst unpredictability and long tails. How would you handle sustained 200 qps with a 100ms SLO?
  - Follow-up to elicit weakness: Ask about per-route dashboards and token-level cost attribution.

- Competitor: Model-monopolist with closed tooling
  - Script: Closed stacks lock you into a single execution path. If you want to change quantization or route to a cheaper variant, how portable are your pipelines?
  - Follow-up: Probe for staging/rollout controls and A/Bing model variants.

- Competitor: Self-host inference vendor
  - Script: Self-host is great if you have ops bandwidth. For teams without a dedicated infra org, how do you handle kernel selection, memory fragmentation, and KV cache invalidation in upgrades?
  - Follow-up: Ask for a real incident postmortem about an upgrade gone wrong.

Core positioning pillars to anchor scripts on (short bullets to memorize):
- Predictable economics: per-route, token-level cost telemetry + Optimize suggestions that reduce unit costs without sacrificing accuracy.
- Deployment parity: same API and rollout semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private options.
- Production reliability: SLA-backed dedicated capacity with graceful fallbacks and canary rollouts.
- Observability for trust: tracing hooks, token timing breakdowns, model regression alerts tied to eval prompts.

Metrics & quick numbers to cite (friendly and conservative):
- Latency: cite median and P95 numbers from our public benchmarks (reference the linked PR); present P95 improvements when KV caching is enabled.
- Cost: quote per-1k token delta pre/post Optimize suggestions (use customer-specific pilot numbers where possible).
- Uptime/SLAs: dedicated commitments vs best-effort hosted.

Objection handling scripts (common customer objections and our short rebuttals):
- Objection: 'We can just use the competitor's cheapest model and be fine.'
  - Response: Cheapest upfront rarely equals cheapest at scale. We model token economics, tail latency, and re-requests — in most pilots we find 15-30% downstream savings after tuning caching and batching.

- Objection: 'We need to use vendor X's model for superior quality.'
  - Response: We don't force a single model. Our value is making model selection operational: run the high-quality model for critical flows and cheaper variants for lower-value requests with automatic routing and fallback.

- Objection: 'Private deployment is too heavy/slow to set up.'
  - Response: We offer a customer-managed control plane with templated on-prem bundles and dedicated onboarding SREs. Typical Private POC is 2–4 weeks for regulated workloads vs months if you build in-house.

- Objection: 'I don't trust your SLAs.'
  - Response: Point to our Dedicated terms and a play: start with a mixed route (hosted + dedicated fallback) for a week to validate tail behavior, then roll dedicated once stable.

Suggested field plays (2–3 step recipes):
- Play A — Cost-savings pilot (3 steps):
  1) Quick baseline: run 48-hour capture on current endpoint (sample payloads).
  2) Redwood Optimize run: surface batching/caching/quantization suggestions and simulate cost impact.
  3) 14-day A/B pilot with routing to cheaper model variants for non-critical prompts. Deliver final commit-level cost delta.

- Play B — Compliance-first proof (3 steps):
  1) Validate private control plane access and KMS integration in a sandbox.
  2) Run an eval set through both hosted and private pathways and collect logs/audit artifacts.
  3) Joint war-room: security + SRE run an attack surface review and finalize deployment checklist.

- Play C — Latency & reliability validation (3 steps):
  1) Synthetic 95th-tail test (gradually ramp to target qps).
  2) Enable KV caching/prefix caching and measure delta.
  3) Stress test failover: simulate region/variant failure and verify fallback meet SLO.

Red-team “gotchas” to drop in deals (things to call out in RFPs / evaluation guides):
- Ask for 95th + 99th percentile numbers under steady state and under ramp, not just median.
- Request per-route cost attribution rather than a blended number.
- Demand description of rollback mechanics for model updates and a sample incident report.
- Require private deployment onboarding timeline and a named SRE support SLA.

Suggested collateral to attach to outbound emails (order matters):
1) One-pager: 'How to validate inference economics in 14 days' (pilot checklist).
2) Short benchmark summary: 'P95 latency and per-token cost delta — Redwood tuned vs raw hosted'.
3) Technical appendix: 'KV cache and quantization primer' (for SEs).

Open items / research requests (for product/benchmarks team):
- Need up-to-date P95/P99 public numbers for the top 4 endpoint vendors across sequence lengths 64/256/1024.
- Collect three anonymized customer pilots showing cost delta after Optimize suggestions.
- Example incident summaries where competitor autoscaling caused customer-visible tail latencies.

Next steps for the AE/SE using this doc:
- Annotate with any customer-specific eval prompts and measurements.
- Attach the baseline capture (stdout from inference logs) to the linked JIRA pilot ticket.
- Run through Play A with first interested prospect and sync learnings in next Tuesday GTM huddle.

Notes to self / copy snippets for Slack and email:
- "Quick pilot idea: 48h capture -> Optimize suggestions -> 14d A/B routing. We usually find 15–30% cost upside"
- "Ask for 95th/99th under load — medians hide the pain."

Owner & escalation: Avery Chen (AE field play owner) — escalate to GTM head Rohit Malhotra for any enterprise procurement questions.
